This directory implements a provider-agnostic AI integration layer for chat, tool/function calling, attachments, embeddings, and prompt templating. It defines shared contracts and enums in `entry.ts`, then supplies base abstractions (`ChatDriver`, `GenericOpenAIChatDriver`, `OpenAIModelEmbeddingDriver`, `IChatWithAttachmentDriver`) that normalize message formats, retries, streaming, constrained JSON output, and error semantics. Provider-specific drivers for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic adapt those abstractions to each vendor SDK and environment configuration. Factories choose appropriate drivers by provider and runtime environment, while utilities format chat history and expand prompt templates for consistent, reusable prompting.

### Key components
`entry.ts` is the shared contract hub: enums (model/provider/roles/verbosity) and interfaces for chat, embeddings, prompts, and factories. `Chat.ts` provides the provider-agnostic `ChatDriver` base and message utilities, while `Chat.GenericOpenAI.ts` concentrates OpenAI-compatible behavior (Responses API config, tool loops, streaming modes, constrained JSON, and error handling). Provider drivers (`Chat.OpenAI.ts`, `Chat.AzureOpenAI.ts`, `Chat.GoogleGemini.ts`, `Chat.Anthropic.ts`) adapt those abstractions to each vendor SDK and environment configuration checks. `ChatFactory.ts` centralizes provider selection, including a NODE_ENV-based default. For multimodal/file workflows, `ChatWithAttachment.ts` defines the attachment/table contract and provider implementations handle inline vs uploaded files; `ChatWithAttachmentFactory.ts` selects them. Embeddings follow the same pattern via `Embed.ts`, provider drivers, and `EmbedFactory.ts`. `DriverHelpers.ts` standardizes retry/backoff and transient error classification across drivers.
